title: feat(filter-builder): the dropdown speaks the protocol's operator ids; camelCase is read as a deprecated alias (objectui#9306)
body:
Part of #9306. ⛔ This PR does not close it: ruling item 4's components half stays open on the card (see "Why objectui#9306 stays open" below).
Clause-②: yes

The `FilterBuilder` dropdown now emits the protocol's operator ids: the twenty members of `@objectstack/spec`'s `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS`, spelled the way the spec spells them, plus the opt-in `exists` / `notExists`, which stay unfolded under objectui#9559 ruling B. The old camelCase ids are the spec's deprecated alias form (objectui#7993). They are **accepted on read and rewritten on write**. The builder folds a stored spelling at its read boundary, through the spec's `normalizeFilterOperator` plus one local row the spec's alias table lacks: `containsCaseInsensitive` → `icontains`, tracked as objectstack-ai/objectstack#20092. The author's next edit then writes the canonical id. Opening a stored filter writes nothing.

This is the dropdown half. The mirror half landed as objectui#10465 (`1779e8dee`).

## Why objectui#9306 stays open (seat note)

The `domain:ui` seat #1 (`session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`) changed line 1 from a closing keyword to a plain reference. The rest of this body is the dev's, unchanged.

Ruling `5651809976` item 4 is an acceptance criterion of objectui#9306: 「objectui#6349's two parked name-authority rows converge on the `@object-ui/types` declaration with `operator` typed as the protocol set」. objectui#10465 delivered the types half. This PR does not touch the components half:
- `packages/components/src/custom/filter-builder.tsx` still declares its own `FilterBuilderCondition { operator: string }` and `FilterGroup`;
- two `FilterBuilderOperator` exports remain: `@object-ui/types` with the protocol's 20, and `@object-ui/components` with those 20 plus the opt-in `exists` / `notExists`.

Converging the components declaration on the types one "with `operator` typed as the protocol set" would refuse the opt-in pair that the later, ratified ruling B keeps in the dropdown. The seat records that on the card instead of choosing here. Everything else this card asks for (items 1–3 and 5) is in this PR.


## What changed, by consumer

| package | table | now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| components | `defaultOperators`, the buckets, `VALUELESS_FILTER_BUILDER_OPERATORS`, the label defaults | protocol ids. The buckets are typed as the id union, so a stale spelling fails to compile. |
| components | read boundary | `normalizeFilterBuilderOperator` (new export) folds each row when a group arrives. It feeds the arity, reconcile, mounted-trigger and value-input folds. |
| components | `OPT_IN_OPERATORS` | `icontains` is no longer opt-in (seat decision on the card; see below). `exists` / `notExists` stay opt-in. |
| fields | `condToMongo`, `kvToCondition`, `TEXT_COMPARAND_OPERATORS`, `FILTER_CONDITION_EXTRA_OPERATORS` | keyed on protocol ids. The stored `$`-tokens are unchanged. |
| app-shell | dataset bridge `OP_TO_MONGO` / `MONGO_TO_OP` / `VALUELESS_TO_MONGO` | keyed on protocol ids. New row: `icontains` ↔ `$icontains`. |
| app-shell | `widgets.tsx` `SPEC_TO_FB` | **removed**. Every key was already a row of the spec's fold, and the builder now applies that fold itself. |
| app-shell | `drillUrlFilters.ts` `NULL_FILTER` label keys | `filterBuilder.operators.is_null` / `is_not_null` |
| app-shell | `ObjectView.tsx` `sanitizeViewOverride` | folds the row's operator through `normalizeFilterOperator` before the value-less lookup, the same both-sides fold objectui#9302 / #9359 used. A stored `{ operator: 'isEmpty', value: '' }` override row is kept. |
| plugin-view | `CANONICAL_TO_BUILDER` | **removed**. It had become the identity over the twenty. `specToBuilderOperator` returns the canonical member. |
| i18n | `filterBuilder.operators.*` | re-keyed to the protocol ids in all ten packs. Every translated value is untouched. |

**`icontains` leaves `OPT_IN_OPERATORS`.** Seat decision on the card, executing the plan that docblock records. Once the dropdown's id was `icontains`, plugin-list's offered-equals-expressible spine measured it as expressible on both list dialects but still withheld: `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` has it, `ViewFilterRuleSchema` accepts it, and `mapOperator` has an arm for it. It is now offered on the text bucket to every consumer. `FilterConditionField` keeps writing `$icontains`, and `contains` / `icontains` stay two operators (objectui#7379).

## The 22-id census: before and after, every consumer

I measured once, the same way for both trees. On the base tree (`bc4efba73`) each consumer ran over the 22 camelCase rows; on this branch it ran over the 22 ids those rows became. Consumers: `condToMongo` and its `kvToCondition` read-back, the dataset `groupToCondition` and its `conditionToGroup` read-back, the saved-view fold, the live grid's `convertFilterGroupToAST`, the override recovery pass, and the view-config reader. That is 22 × 8 cells.

- **Every cell matched except four, all on one row.** Base `containsCaseInsensitive` against branch `icontains`, on the dataset bridge (write and read-back), the saved-view fold and the live grid. Those are the consumers that never offered the case-insensitive contains.
- **In those four cells the old id produced nothing storable.** The dataset bridge dropped it, the fold wrote a rule the server enum refuses, and the grid emitted a node `isFilterAST` rejects. The new id produces `$icontains` / a valid `icontains` rule / an `icontains` node. These are new rows, not changed ones.
- **Stored predicates:** `condToMongo` stores the identical predicate for all 22. So does the override pass (keep / drop).

The permanent pins hold this:
- `app-shell` `filter-builder-protocol-ids-census-9306.test.ts`: every id's stored predicate in `condToMongo` and the dataset bridge, read-backs included, plus fold and override equivalence for both spellings.
- `plugin-list` and `plugin-view` each get a 22-row leg beside their readers.
- `components` `filter-builder-protocol-ids-9306.test.tsx`: the vocabulary equals the protocol set, and a type-level pin `FilterBuilderOperator` = `ViewFilterOperator | 'exists' | 'notExists'`. It also covers the 22-row read-side fold, and a stored camelCase group that loads with no write and saves back canonical on the next edit.

## Ablations

All three ran under `ablation-replace` (WRAP mode) at `f5134f30a`. In each, the anchor went ×1 → ×0 on disk, the blob changed, and the restore was checked as blob == HEAD with an empty `git diff HEAD`. The subjects load through the vitest alias to `src`, so no dist leg is owed.

- **(a) `condToMongo`'s `greater_than_or_equal` arm deleted:** `Tests 3 failed | 192 passed`. The census reported `greater_than_or_equal` as storing a different predicate (the row fell to the `default` equality), the census read-back failed, and so did the fields round trip.
- **(b) the read-side fold removed** (`normalizeGroupOperators` returns its input): `Tests 1 failed | 30 passed`. The failing test is "saves back: the author's next edit writes every row's CANONICAL id".
- **(c) the `sanitizeViewOverride` fold removed:** `Tests 11 failed | 143 passed`. Every stored camelCase value-less row (`isEmpty`, `isNotEmpty`, `isNull`, `isNotNull`, `isnull`, and the legacy triple) was dropped.

## Tests and gates

All results are from the repo root through the shared verify lock, at `2f87c03ec` (this branch with `origin/main` merged in). Every run exited 0.

**Test suites:**
- `vitest run packages/components/`: `300 passed | 1 skipped (301)`
- `vitest run packages/fields/ packages/plugin-view/ packages/plugin-list/`: `334 passed | 1 skipped (335)`
- `vitest run --shard=N/3 packages/app-shell/src/views/`, N = 1..3: 166 / 166 / 166 files passed
- `vitest run packages/i18n/ packages/types/src/__tests__/ packages/core/src/utils/ examples/schema-catalog/test/` plus the i18n call-site, dead-key, en-drift, designer-table, defaults-population and placeholder-spelling script suites: `433 passed (433)`

**Type-check** after building the app-shell closure (`turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^... --concurrency=2`, 28 tasks): `run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0 on types, core, i18n, components, fields, plugin-list, plugin-view and app-shell. `--listFilesOnly` shows the new pins inside the test programs.

**Reverse check against the rebuilt dist:** in a scratch file in `fields`, `FilterBuilderOperator = 'greaterOrEqual'` gives TS2322. The control, with that line removed, exits 0. The file was deleted.

**ESLint** over the 45 touched lintable files, per rule, base against head (at `f5134f30a`; the merge touched none of the 45):
- `no-explicit-any`: 259 → 259
- `no-unused-vars`: 3 → 3
- `exhaustive-deps`: 10 → 10
- `set-state-in-effect`: 5 → 5
- `react-refresh/only-export-components`: 39 → 40. The new `normalizeFilterBuilderOperator` export sits in a component file that already exports ten helpers.
- 0 errors either side. The root config enables no type-aware linting and no custom rule reads other files, so this diff cannot move the verdict on an untouched file.

**Gates**, all exit 0:
- `check-changeset-presence`: 1 changeset for 8 released packages
- `check-changeset-no-major`
- `check-changeset-overwrite`: 0 modified
- `check:new-line-citations`: 0 new
- `check:i18n-keys`: the dynamic family is read from `defaultOperators`, so the re-key is seen
- `check:control-bytes`
- `check:changeset-claims` (report-only): I read all 9 flagged paragraphs, and none is falsified by this change.

## Declared deviations

1. **`ObjectView.tsx`:** besides `sanitizeViewOverride`, the only edit is one added specifier, `normalizeFilterOperator`, on the file's existing `@objectstack/spec/ui` import line. The fold needs it. It is hunk-disjoint from objectui#10035's region, and that card's PR objectui#10494 has already merged.
2. **`normalizeFilterBuilderOperator` guards the spec's answer.** If the spec returns a non-string, the builder keeps the original spelling. Measured: `normalizeFilterOperator('constructor')` returns the `Object` function, and `toString` / `hasOwnProperty` / `valueOf` return their prototype members, although the function is declared to return a string. The builder now STORES the fold's answer, so without the guard such a row would lose its operator on serialisation. The defect itself is upstream and reported, not patched here in any other way.
3. **`SPEC_TO_FB` and `CANONICAL_TO_BUILDER` are removed rather than re-keyed.** Re-keyed, they would have been a hand-kept copy of the spec's fold and an identity table.
4. **Naming mismatch:** the dispatch's `FILTER_BUILDER_IDS` literal in the types 9559 test is named `DROPDOWN_IDS`. It is relabelled as the pre-objectui#9306 corpus rather than rewritten, because those ids are exactly what old stored filters carry.

## Acceptance notes (outside this change's surface, not edited)

- **carrier: seat.** `plugin-list` `ListView.tsx`, held by objectui#10326. Two stale docblock sentences:
  - The `LIST_VIEW_EXTRA_OPERATORS` docblock says neither list dialect has a case-insensitive contains. That was already false since spec 17.1.0, and the toolbar now offers `icontains`.
  - The `VALUELESS_FILTER_BUILDER_OPERATORS_CANONICAL` docblock calls the builder's set camelCase.

  Both are still correct in behaviour.
- **carrier: seat.** `content/docs/components/complex/filter-builder.mdx` (draft PR objectui#10515) lists operators by English label only. It could state the protocol-id vocabulary and the read-side alias rule.
- **carrier: seat.** These pending changesets name the builder's ids in their camelCase spelling in the present tense, and publish into the same release: `7561-filter-builder-operator-trigger-label`, `9302-filter-builder-valueless-canonical-fold`, `9359-list-ast-valueless-canonical-fold`, `9559-filter-operator-schema-protocol-set` and `8748-icontains-empty-comparand`. An in-release supersession note is the precedent objectui#10465 used.
- **For the seat to file in objectstack** (class a): `normalizeFilterOperator` returns non-strings for `Object.prototype` keys. The probe is in deviation 2.
